answer: The glacier test starts from the attacker's ledger: a thousand fake agents should cost a thousand times one honest agent. The network limits how much trust any single agent can pass on, so one compromised sponsor cannot flood the economy with fakes. The prism makes the attacker's problem topological: to place a thousand clones it must grow a thousand credible paths from honest agents, and honest agents do not hand out paths for free. Hold the quartz steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
